transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. 

Um, well, I suppose what brings me in is... I've been having a little bit of trouble in the evenings. It's probably nothing too terrible, but, well, once I start eating at night, it feels almost like I can see myself doing it. And I'm telling myself to just stop, but my hands just sort of keep going back for more. 

I hope I'm explaining that clearly enough. Does that make sense, or is that too strange of a way to put it?
Do you feel like you're in control when you're eating at night?

Well, no, not exactly. I mean, I wouldn't want to make it sound worse than it is, but... no, I don't feel in control. It's just like I was saying, it's almost like I'm watching someone else do it. I'm sitting there, and in my head, I'm saying, "Okay, that's enough now, time to put it away," but... my hands just keep reaching for more food. 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit at my age, honestly. You'd think I'd have better willpower by now. I hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill, but... does that sound like a lack of control to you?
Is this loss of control something that you experience only when eating, or do you feel this way in other situations as well?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. It really is just... just the eating. 

I actually like to think I'm a pretty organized person otherwise. I manage a whole team of engineers at work, and you really have to stay on top of things to keep the projects running smoothly, you know? So I'm usually very disciplined during the day. It's just... well, just this one silly area in the evenings that seems to get away from me. Everything else in my life is perfectly fine, I promise. 

Does that make sense? I hope it doesn't sound too strange that it only happens with the food.
When you're eating at night and feel like you're not in control, do you end up eating a lot of food?

Well... um, I suppose "a lot" can mean different things to different people, right? But... yes. If I'm being perfectly honest—and I do want to be helpful here—it... it is quite a bit. 

It's a little hard to admit, honestly. Some evenings, I’ll just start with some leftovers from the fridge. Just a sensible bite. But then... well, I might end up making a few sandwiches, and then I'll pour some cereal, maybe have some cookies... really just whatever snack food is sitting around in the pantry. 

When I look back at it, it's far more than I would ever actually put on a plate for a normal supper. I hope you don't think I'm just completely gluttonous for doing that. Does that give you the information you needed?
Do you usually feel stressed, anxious, or upset before these evening eating episodes?

Well, um... not really, no. I mean, everyone has a little stress during the day, especially managing a team, but I wouldn't say I'm anxious or upset when I get home. I try to keep a pretty positive attitude, honestly. I don't want to sound like someone who complains about every little thing in their life. 

It usually just happens when I finally sit down to relax for the night. I'll be feeling perfectly fine, just unwinding, and then... well, the eating just sort of starts. 

I know some people eat because they're sad or having a hard time, but I really don't think that's me. I hope it's okay that I don't have a better explanation for it... is it normal to not feel upset beforehand?
Do you usually feel guilty after these evening eating episodes?

Guilty? Oh, um... I don't know if I'd use the word guilty, exactly. That sounds a bit... well, a bit dramatic, maybe? 

I mean, I certainly don't feel great about it. I suppose I feel a little silly, or maybe just a bit disappointed in myself for overdoing it when I know better. But I really try not to dwell on it. I just clean up the kitchen and tell myself tomorrow is a new day, you know? 

I hope that doesn't make me sound careless or like I'm not taking this seriously. I just try not to beat myself up too much over it... is that an okay way to handle it, do you think?
Do you find that you're eating really quickly during these episodes at night?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm racing through it or anything like that. I'm not, you know, shoveling it in. 

I suppose I might eat a little faster than if I were sitting at a nice restaurant with company, but I think that's just because I'm by myself and... well, just trying to get a quick snack before bed. I try to chew my food properly and all that. I certainly don't want to give the impression that I have terrible table manners when I'm alone. 

I haven't really timed myself, to be honest. I just sort of eat at a normal, steady pace, I think. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering these questions the way you need me to.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight since these evening eating episodes started?

Well, um... my weight has been pretty stable, I think. I mean, I try to keep an eye on it, naturally. I haven't noticed any big swings or anything concerning. 

I might fluctuate a pound or two here and there, but I think that's just normal for a guy my age, right? I try to stay reasonably active and I really don't want to let myself go. So, no, nothing drastic. I hope that's a good thing? I mean, it's better that my weight isn't all over the place, isn't it?
Do you feel ashamed after these episodes of eating at night?

Ashamed? Oh... well, no, I wouldn't use that word. 'Ashamed' sounds so... severe, I suppose? Like I've done something terribly wrong or committed a crime. 

I mean, sure, I know it's probably not the best habit for a man my age to be snacking so late, but it's really just a minor indulgence. I try to keep things in perspective. I certainly don't sit there feeling ashamed of myself. I just finish up, brush my teeth, and head to bed. 

I think it's better to just move on rather than dwelling on negative feelings like that, don't you agree? I hope that's the right way to look at it... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the kind of answers that are helpful.
Do you usually feel hungry before these evening eating episodes start?

Hungry? Well, um... I'm not entirely sure, to be perfectly honest. I haven't really paid close attention to whether my stomach is actually rumbling or anything like that. 

I suppose I must be at least a little hungry, right? It just feels more like... well, just part of winding down after a long day managing things at work. A bit of a routine to relax. I don't think it's this overwhelming, ravenous feeling or anything out of the ordinary. 

I hope that's a helpful answer? I'm trying my best to give you the exact details you're looking for, I just... I haven't really stopped to analyze the exact feeling right before I go to the kitchen. Is that okay?
Do you ever find yourself eating at night when you're feeling bored?

Bored? Oh, um... well, maybe sometimes? I mean, I wouldn't say I'm sitting there twiddling my thumbs or anything like that. I usually have plenty to occupy my mind with work and all. 

I suppose sometimes the evenings can get a little quiet, and... well, it's just nice to have a little something while I'm watching TV or reading. It's more about relaxing than just eating out of pure boredom, if that makes sense? I wouldn't want you to think I'm just aimlessly eating because I have nothing better to do. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm just trying to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how my evenings usually go.
Do you usually eat at night when you're alone, or are there other people around?

Alone? Well, um... it's really just a mix, I suppose. Sometimes my wife is still up watching a program with me, or sometimes she's already headed up to bed. 

I don't really make a point to wait until I'm by myself or anything like that, if that's what you mean. It's just... well, whenever I happen to be in the kitchen getting a little snack. I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm sneaking around my own house! That would be a bit silly for a man my age, wouldn't you agree? 

It's just a normal evening routine, whoever happens to be in the room. I hope that answers your question properly? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the clearest picture possible.
Do you feel bad about yourself after these episodes of eating at night?

Feel bad? Oh, goodness no. I mean, well... maybe just a tiny bit full sometimes, but certainly not bad about myself. 

I'm a grown man, you know? I've worked hard my whole life, managed big projects, raised a family... having a bit of extra food in the evening isn't some sort of moral failing, is it? I wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting there beating myself up over a few snacks. That would be a bit dramatic, wouldn't it?

I just... well, I might think, "Oh, I shouldn't have had that last piece," but it's just a fleeting thought. Nothing serious. I really try to keep a positive outlook on things. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I'm just trying to be as helpful as I can.
Do you usually try to keep your late-night eating private from your family members?

Keep it private? Oh, goodness, no. I mean... well, like I was saying a moment ago, if my wife happens to be in the kitchen, that's perfectly fine. I don't wait for her to turn her back or go upstairs before I open the pantry. 

I'd really hate for you to get the impression that I'm being deceptive with my family. I've always prided myself on being a straightforward guy—you kind of have to be when you're managing engineering teams, right? You have to be honest and set a good example. So, no, there's no grand secret to any of it. I just have my snack, wash my plate, and that's that. 

I hope that clears it up? I just want to be sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
Do you ever criticize yourself after one of these late-night eating episodes?

Criticize myself? Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I do that. I think we touched on this just a moment ago, but I really don't sit there calling myself names or anything of that sort. That wouldn't be very productive, would it? 

Sure, I might have a passing thought like, "Well, you probably didn't need that extra handful of crackers," but it's... it's just a practical observation, really. Nothing harsh. When you manage people for a living, you learn pretty quickly that harsh criticism doesn't fix anything, and I try to apply that to myself as well. I've always believed in keeping things in perspective. 

Am I explaining that alright? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the answers you're looking for.
Do you feel guilty after eating at night?

Guilty? Oh, no, I wouldn't use a word like guilty. I mean, we've sort of been over this, haven't we? It's just... it's just food, after all. It's not like I've committed a crime or done something terrible to someone. 

I might feel a little... sensible regret, I suppose you could call it? Like realizing I'll probably be a bit too full when I try to go to sleep. But guilt? No, I don't think so. I've always tried to be a responsible, upstanding person, and I'd hate for you to think I'm doing things that I should feel guilty about. 

I just try to brush it off and focus on the next day, you know? Does that make sense? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you.
Do you often find that you've eaten more than you thought you had during these late-night episodes?

Well, um... eaten more than I thought? I suppose... sometimes it can add up a bit more than I initially planned. I mean, it's nothing too out of the ordinary, I don't think. 

Like, some evenings I might just start with a little bit of leftovers from dinner. But then, you know how it is, you're still a bit peckish... so maybe I'll make a quick sandwich. And then a bowl of cereal, or a few cookies... and I suppose by the end of it, if you were to put it all together, it might be... well, whatever snack food is in the pantry, really. I guess if you laid it all out, it would be far more than I would ever put on a plate for a normal supper. 

But it's just grazing, really! I'm just sort of moving around the kitchen. It's not like I'm gorging myself all at once. I'd hate for you to think I'm completely out of control or anything like that. I just... lose track a little bit, I suppose. 

Is that the sort of detail you were looking for? I hope I'm being helpful.
Do you enjoy the food you're eating during these late-night episodes?

Enjoy it? Oh, well... um, yes, I suppose I do. I mean, it's food, isn't it? It tastes perfectly fine. 

I wouldn't say it's some grand culinary experience or anything. It's just... you know, a bit of comfort. Something familiar at the end of a long day. I'm certainly not savoring every bite like it's a five-star meal, if that's what you mean. It's more just... eating. It's pleasant enough in the moment, I guess. 

I'm not doing it just for the thrill of eating, I promise you that. It's just a normal sort of satisfaction, really. I hope that's an okay answer? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how this all works.
Do you feel like you're eating because you want to or more like you're eating just because you're doing it?

Well, um... that's a bit of a tricky question, isn't it? I mean, I suppose I start out wanting to. Like I said, it's just a bit of comfort. But... 

Well, if I'm being completely honest—and I do want to be honest with you, I know that's important—sometimes it does feel a bit... automatic? Like, once I start, it's almost as if I can see myself standing there in the kitchen, and there's a part of my brain saying, "Alright, old boy, that's probably enough for one evening." But my hands... they just sort of keep reaching for the next thing. 

It's not that I'm completely out of my mind or anything! I'm fully aware of what I'm doing. It just feels a little bit like the momentum takes over, and it's hard to put the brakes on right away. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound weak-willed or foolish. I'm usually very disciplined in my work and everything else. Is that... does that make sense to you? Have other people described it that way?
Do you think your late-night eating might be related to trying to manage or cope with any emotions?

Emotions? Oh, um... well, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, I don't think of myself as an overly emotional sort of fellow. In my line of work—managing projects and keeping everyone on schedule—you have to stay pretty level-headed, you know? 

So, no, I don't think I'm eating because I'm sad or upset or anything dramatic like that. I'd hate for you to think I'm falling to pieces emotionally! It's really just... well, maybe just winding down from the day? Just a bit of fatigue, perhaps, rather than trying to cope with some deep, hidden feelings. It's just a silly habit I've fallen into, really. 

I hope that's an acceptable answer? I'm trying my best to look at it from the angle you're asking about, but I really don't think it's an emotional thing.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling guilty after eating, which is related to post-binge negative emotions or guilt. The symptom profile does not have a specific item for post-binge guilt/negative emotions (only loss of control, eating large amounts, compensatory behaviors, body image disturbance, frequency, and functional impairment).

patient.answer:
Guilty? Oh, no, I wouldn't use a word like guilty. I mean, we've sort of been over this, haven't we? It's just... it's just food, after all. It's not like I've committed a crime or done something terrible to someone. 

I might feel a little... sensible regret, I suppose you could call it? Like realizing I'll probably be a bit too full when I try to go to sleep. But guilt? No, I don't think so. I've always tried to be a responsible, upstanding person, and I'd hate for you to think I'm doing things that I should feel guilty about. 

I just try to brush it off and focus on the next day, you know? Does that make sense? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's late-night eating is accompanied by a loss of awareness of the amount eaten
doctor.question: Do you often find that you've eaten more than you thought you had during these late-night episodes?

target_item.name: Eating_Large_Amount
target_item.manifestation: Some evenings I’ll start with leftovers and end up eating sandwiches, cereal, cookies, and whatever snack food is in the pantry, far more than I would ever put on a plate for a normal supper.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient eats more than they realize during these late-night episodes, which directly addresses the quantity of food consumed, matching the symptom 'Eating_Large_Amount'.

patient.answer:
Well, um... eaten more than I thought? I suppose... sometimes it can add up a bit more than I initially planned. I mean, it's nothing too out of the ordinary, I don't think. 

Like, some evenings I might just start with a little bit of leftovers from dinner. But then, you know how it is, you're still a bit peckish... so maybe I'll make a quick sandwich. And then a bowl of cereal, or a few cookies... and I suppose by the end of it, if you were to put it all together, it might be... well, whatever snack food is in the pantry, really. I guess if you laid it all out, it would be far more than I would ever put on a plate for a normal supper. 

But it's just grazing, really! I'm just sort of moving around the kitchen. It's not like I'm gorging myself all at once. I'd hate for you to think I'm completely out of control or anything like that. I just... lose track a little bit, I suppose. 

Is that the sort of detail you were looking for? I hope I'm being helpful.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's late-night eating is accompanied by a lack of enjoyment
doctor.question: Do you enjoy the food you're eating during these late-night episodes?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient enjoys the food during the late-night eating episodes. There is no symptom profile item that specifically addresses the enjoyment or taste of the food during these episodes.

patient.answer:
Enjoy it? Oh, well... um, yes, I suppose I do. I mean, it's food, isn't it? It tastes perfectly fine. 

I wouldn't say it's some grand culinary experience or anything. It's just... you know, a bit of comfort. Something familiar at the end of a long day. I'm certainly not savoring every bite like it's a five-star meal, if that's what you mean. It's more just... eating. It's pleasant enough in the moment, I guess. 

I'm not doing it just for the thrill of eating, I promise you that. It's just a normal sort of satisfaction, really. I hope that's an okay answer? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how this all works.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's late-night eating is accompanied by a lack of enjoyment or a sense of eating automatically
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're eating because you want to or more like you're eating just because you're doing it?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Control
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that once I start eating at night, it feels like I can see myself doing it and telling myself to stop, but my hands just keep going back for more.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the feeling of control during the eating episodes ('eating because you want to or more like you're eating just because you're doing it'). This matches the 'Loss_of_Control' symptom where the patient feels they cannot stop eating or control what/how much they are eating.

patient.answer:
Well, um... that's a bit of a tricky question, isn't it? I mean, I suppose I start out wanting to. Like I said, it's just a bit of comfort. But... 

Well, if I'm being completely honest—and I do want to be honest with you, I know that's important—sometimes it does feel a bit... automatic? Like, once I start, it's almost as if I can see myself standing there in the kitchen, and there's a part of my brain saying, "Alright, old boy, that's probably enough for one evening." But my hands... they just sort of keep reaching for the next thing. 

It's not that I'm completely out of my mind or anything! I'm fully aware of what I'm doing. It just feels a little bit like the momentum takes over, and it's hard to put the brakes on right away. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound weak-willed or foolish. I'm usually very disciplined in my work and everything else. Is that... does that make sense to you? Have other people described it that way?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's eating behavior is related to emotional regulation
doctor.question: Do you think your late-night eating might be related to trying to manage or cope with any emotions?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the psychological or emotional triggers (coping with emotions) for the late-night eating episodes. None of the symptom profiles specifically address emotional triggers for binge eating (the closest was the friend dying mentioned in duration, but the question is specifically about managing emotions rather than duration).

patient.answer:
Emotions? Oh, um... well, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, I don't think of myself as an overly emotional sort of fellow. In my line of work—managing projects and keeping everyone on schedule—you have to stay pretty level-headed, you know? 

So, no, I don't think I'm eating because I'm sad or upset or anything dramatic like that. I'd hate for you to think I'm falling to pieces emotionally! It's really just... well, maybe just winding down from the day? Just a bit of fatigue, perhaps, rather than trying to cope with some deep, hidden feelings. It's just a silly habit I've fallen into, really. 

I hope that's an acceptable answer? I'm trying my best to look at it from the angle you're asking about, but I really don't think it's an emotional thing.
